title: Lesson 3.4 — Phonemic Awareness
source: User-supplied WGU course lesson and guided practice, November 2026
overview: Phonemic awareness is a subset of phonological awareness involving individual speech sounds, without needing printed words. The supplied figure orders broad awareness skills and phoneme-level skills by increasing complexity.

skills.description: Identify an individual speech sound at the beginning, middle or end of a word.
Break a spoken word into ordered phonemes.
Combine individual phonemes to make a whole word.
Add a phoneme to form another word.
Remove a phoneme to form another word.

instructional_note: The supplied lesson recommends approximately 3 minutes of phonological-processor activation aligned to the day's phoneme-grapheme learning, followed by teacher modeling and letter connections. Treat duration as a lesson recommendation, not a universal requirement.
distinction_note: The lesson's Science of Reading paragraph says phonemic awareness 'is the alphabetic principle'; these are related but distinct. Phonemic awareness concerns spoken phonemes; the alphabetic principle concerns their representation in print. Keep the source wording noted rather than teaching these as identical.

guided_practice.prompt: Select all the attributes of Phonemic Awareness from the list shown below:
guided_practice.feedback_correct: Isolation identifies individual sounds; segmenting separates phonemes; blending combines them; addition/deletion/substitution manipulate phonemes.
